title: William Norton's New Guide Explores the World of UFOs and UAPs

content:
Drawing on the history of UFO research, the book examines investigations, science, government programs, terminology, and unexplained cases.

New York City, New York, United States, 14th Sep 2026 - Author and UFO researcher William Norton introduces The Realm of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena: A Researcher's Reference Guide to UFOs, an extensive reference work created for readers seeking a deeper understanding of the history, terminology, investigations, technologies, theories, and unresolved questions surrounding unidentified aerial phenomena.

Developed from Norton's experience as a MUFON field investigator, the book was conceived as an encyclopedia-style resource that could serve as a practical reference for researchers investigating UFO and UAP reports. Rather than presenting the subject through a single narrative, Norton brings together a broad range of subjects that researchers may encounter while studying unexplained aerial phenomena.

The book explores hundreds of subjects across the UFO and UAP field, including historic incidents, investigative organizations, government programs, military and intelligence activities, aerospace technology, scientific concepts, terminology, research methodologies, and competing explanations for unusual observations. Its extensive alphabetical organization allows readers to use the book as a research reference while exploring individual subjects or following connections between related topics.

Among the areas addressed are Project Blue Book, AATIP, UAPTF, UAP terminology, government classification, radar and photographic evidence, aerospace technology, transmedium phenomena, scientific methodology, unidentified submerged objects, time and space theories, and numerous historical UFO cases.

Norton emphasizes the importance of approaching UAP research from multiple disciplines. The manuscript considers scientific, technological, historical, military, paranormal, and theoretical perspectives, reflecting the wide range of subjects that can arise during an investigation.

Rather than claiming to provide a definitive answer to every unexplained phenomenon, The Realm of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena is presented as a foundation for continued research. Norton acknowledges that information surrounding UAPs can change as new evidence becomes available and encourages readers to approach the subject as an evolving area of investigation.

The book is intended for UFO and UAP enthusiasts, field investigators, researchers, students, science and technology readers, and anyone interested in examining the history and unanswered questions surrounding unidentified aerial phenomena. The work is particularly positioned as a reference for readers who want to move beyond isolated UFO stories and gain familiarity with the broader terminology, organizations, investigations, and theories that define the field.
About the Book
The Realm of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena: A Researcher's Reference Guide to UFOs is an encyclopedia-style research reference examining the terminology, history, investigations, technologies, scientific concepts, government programs, theories, and unresolved cases associated with UFOs and UAPs. The book is designed to provide readers with a broad foundation for exploring one of the worlds most persistent and debated unexplained phenomena.
About the Author
William Norton is a researcher and UFO investigator whose experience in the field contributed to the development of The Realm of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena. His work as a MUFON field investigator helped identify the need for a comprehensive reference resource that could bring together the diverse terminology, concepts, historical cases, investigative approaches, and research material encountered during UAP investigations. The resulting book reflects his effort to create an accessible research tool for both newcomers and experienced investigators.
